commit.message:
feat(ui): UX-02 slice 2 — finish SectionLabel adoption across Settings Seven exact-equivalent conversions in five files, completing `app/(app)/settings/`. Continues #746's slice 1 (Settings > Availability) with the same mechanism, the same convergence-stop architecture, and no change to the primitive. WHY THIS BOUNDARY. The slice was drawn around a DIRECTORY rather than around the largest files, because a completed directory is a stronger claim than a count. "Seven more conversions" is bookkeeping that needs maintaining; "no file under Settings hand-rolls this label" is a property a reader can check. The remaining backlog is deliberately untouched: calendar 23, components/* 21, session charting 13, client profile 8, records 2, dashboard 2. EVERY CONVERSION IS BYTE-EQUIVALENT. Both sizes already exist on the primitive — `text-xs` is size="section", `text-[11px]` is size="caption" — and `as` carries the original element where it was not a span. No new size, no new tone, no new primitive, and no typography widened. BookingLinkCard.tsx

-> as="p" ConsentTemplatesEditor.tsx

-> as="h3" size="caption" intake/page.tsx -> (defaults) services/page.tsx

-> as="h3" services/page.tsx -> size="caption" TrackingProviderSelector x2 -> (defaults) VARIANTS ARE LEFT ALONE, 2 in services/page.tsx and 2 in TrackingProviderSelector.tsx. That is slice 1's precedent — it left 4, 1, 0 and 2 behind in its own four files — and it is the point of the exact-equivalence bar: those spellings differ from the primitive, so converting them would be a visual decision this lane is not authorized to make. RE-DERIVED AGAINST a476f9e6, NOT ASSUMED. The recensus that selected this slice ran against 4e8ea7ae; production moved twice before implementation. Re-running the census on the new tree returned the identical 76/33 with the same seven call sites at the same lines, so the scope held — but it was checked rather than carried forward. Census: 76 -> 69 exact duplicates, 33 -> 28 files, ZERO under Settings. THE NEW GUARD LIMB IS SMALLER THAN IT FIRST LOOKED, AND SAYS SO. I wrote test 5 claiming it catches a new Settings file that hand-rolls the label. It does not catch anything test 3b would miss — 3b walks every file and skips only the primitive and the baseline, so any new file is already an offender there. The comment now states what is actually its own: failing BY NAME on the slice's headline claim, and the contradiction check that nothing else makes — a root declared complete must have no legacy baseline rows left inside it, or the two tables can disagree and the stale row re-permits what COMPLETED_ROOT forbids. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)

Merge production 93acbe1b into UX-02 slice 2

Normal merge of current production. No rebase, no squash, no force push.
Automatic merge, zero conflicts: production touched 27 files and none of
them is in this slice, so there was nothing to resolve and nothing to
choose between.

SCOPE VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. All six files this PR changes are
byte-identical to the pre-merge head 61250f95 -- the five Settings surfaces
and the section-label-adoption source guard. SectionLabel usage across
app/(app)/settings is unchanged at 68 occurrences, so the merge neither
widened nor narrowed the adoption. No primitive, typography, motion,
navigation or performance file entered through it, and no clinical
semantics were touched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Merge production 369e2d30 (#771 waitlist Twilio Verify) into UX-02 slice 2

test(ui): retire the directory-wide completion claim, and pin the blind spot that hid it

Codex P2 at 934e89e4, and it is correct. TEST/GUARD ONLY — the seven UI
conversions are untouched, and no further Settings page is converted.

WHAT WAS WRONG. Test 5 asserted `app/(app)/settings/` was COMPLETE. It is not,
and the assertion could not have discovered that: `isHandRolledDuplicate` rejects
any class list carrying an extra utility, so two labels spelling the primitive's
typography beside layout classes were invisible to it and the directory read as
finished.

  services/page.tsx:70   scroll-mt-24 …
  services/page.tsx:237  cursor-pointer select-none px-3 py-2 …

BROADENING THE DETECTOR WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IS NOT SAFE HERE.
Tolerating extras wholesale raises the count in six more files — calendar/[id]/
page.tsx alone goes 14 -> 16, and five files not on the baseline at all start
tripping rule 3b. The guard could then only be kept green by converting them,
which is exactly the directory-wide conversion this PR is not doing. The
allowlist it would need is 14 classes wide and includes `hover:text-neutral-700`
and `dark:hover:text-neutral-300` — COLOURS the primitive does not have.
Tolerating those would call a hover-tinted label "the primitive" and be wrong on
the merits, not merely broad. So the claim shrank instead.

WHAT THE GUARD NOW SAYS, WHICH IS ONLY WHAT THIS PR PROVES:
  * the nine selected files use the primitive, at 28 sites (tests 1, 2, 2b);
  * no converted site regressed (test 2);
  * the detector's blind spot is REAL and stated (test 5);
  * the remaining census is explicitly NOT claimed empty, and is a FLOOR rather
    than a total (test 5b).

The suite title moved from "across Settings" to "at the selected Settings sites"
for the same reason — it was the last piece of completion language left.

THE REGRESSION CONTROL is the exact shape the finding named, asserted three ways
so it cannot pass hollow: the shape really does spell the primitive's typography;
the detector really does ignore it; and stripping ONLY `scroll-mt-24` makes the
same detector report it — without that third limb the second is satisfied by a
detector that returns false for everything.

5b IS SCOPED TO SETTINGS BECAUSE THE WHOLE-TREE VERSION WAS FLAKY. A second
full-tree AST pass measured 2.6-5.4s against vitest's 5s default and failed on
the slow runs. A guard that reds on machine load teaches people to re-run it,
which is worse than not having it. Now 1.5s, stable across repeated runs.

`isHandRolledDuplicate` and `hasPrimitiveTypography` are extracted from
`duplicates()` so the limit can be asserted on a literal directly, rather than
inferred from a file scan.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(ui): the undercount control matched lookalikes, not duplicates

Codex P2 at f8a97d7e, and the defect is in my own repair rather than in the code
it was repairing. TEST/GUARD ONLY.

WHAT WAS WRONG. 5b decided a file "undercounts" using
`hasPrimitiveTypography(l) && !isHandRolledDuplicate(l)` — that is "shares
font-medium uppercase tracking-wider and is not an exact duplicate", which is a
far larger set than "is a duplicate the detector cannot see". Measured in
Settings, it matches EIGHT literals of which only TWO are real:

  REAL   scroll-mt-24 text-xs … text-neutral-500          (services/page.tsx)
  REAL   cursor-pointer select-none px-3 py-2 text-xs …   (services/page.tsx)
  not    text-sm … text-neutral-500                       (off-scale size)
  not    … text-[10px] … text-emerald-800                 (status pill)
  not    … text-[10px] … text-neutral-500                 (status pill)
  not    font-medium uppercase tracking-wider text-neutral-500 (no size at all)

So once the two real ones are converted, 5b would have stayed green on the
remaining six and gone on asserting that the census undercounts when nothing was
being missed. The control would have outlived the thing it controls — which is
the failure mode it was written to prevent.

THE FIX IS A PRECISE PREDICATE, NOT A WIDER ONE. `isLayoutDecoratedDuplicate` is
`isHandRolledDuplicate` with its "and nothing else" clause inverted: the
primitive's FULL contract — typography, exactly one contract size, a muted tone —
plus extras. No generic Tailwind parsing; the same CONTRACT read from the
primitive, one clause different.

It now falls to zero the moment the last layout-decorated duplicate is adopted,
and 5b reds at that point — telling whoever did it that the detector can be
tightened and this control retired. That is what the comment always promised and
what the loose predicate could not deliver.

Two assertions were added to the control so the distinction cannot quietly
regress: the pinned shape must satisfy the precise predicate, and a status pill
(`bg-emerald-100 … text-[10px] … text-emerald-800`) must NOT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Merge production a5e179f2 (#770 ONB-03 dashboard readiness) into UX-02 slice 2

feat(ui): UX-02 slice 3 — finish SectionLabel adoption across session charting

`components/ui/section-label.tsx` owns the uppercase section label. Thirteen
call sites across the session-charting directory spelled its class list out by
hand; this slice replaces them with the primitive and retires their baseline
entries. The remaining census goes 69 -> 56.

Scope was DERIVED, not chosen. The population comes from the guard's own
predicate read out of the primitive — typography, exactly one contract size, a
muted tone, and nothing else — so every converted site was already proved to
carry no information the primitive lacks. The directory holds thirteen `.tsx`
files and the other eight contain no `uppercase` at all, which is what makes
these five the whole surface rather than a subset.

WHY THIS SURFACE. It is the only remaining candidate that reaches zero of BOTH
detector shapes: no exact duplicates and no layout-decorated ones. Calendar
holds the larger population (23) and cannot finish — two decorated labels stay
behind in `calendar/[id]/page.tsx` — and it is baselined T2, which buys a
heavier lane than a label swap needs. A `components/**` slice pulls the payment
lane on one filename and has a `<label>` host the primitive's `as=` union does
not cover. This diff is T1, lanes application + browser_core.

EQUIVALENCE, stated precisely. Every host tag is preserved via `as=`; there is
no `<div>` in the population, so nothing moves between block and inline, and no
site carried an attribute beyond `className`. `text-neutral-500` becomes the
primitive's `text-fg-muted`: `--color-fg-muted` is `oklch(55.6% 0 0)`, defined
exactly once, and Hone's `dark` variant maps to a `.dark` class that is never
applied — so the computed colour is identical in every reachable theme. The
class STRING does change, so the guard's claims are about adoption and the
absence of duplicates, never about byte-identical output.

Baseline entries are DELETED rather than commented out. Rule 3a-bis exists
because a surviving entry keeps its allowance: a stub saying "this path may hold
N" would let every retired duplicate return and still pass.

The table's ownership note is removed rather than refreshed. It attributed two
files to another open PR, that attribution had already gone stale, and a count
table is the wrong place to track branch state.

Verification: guard 26/26; both halves proved non-vacuous by mutation — a
reintroduced duplicate reds rule 2, and restoring a retired entry reds rule 3a;
`tsc --noEmit` clean; 57 affected test files, 1041 tests pass; lint introduces
zero new messages, confirmed by linting the base content of the two files that
carry pre-existing unused-var warnings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
